Maya (Support): FYI customer Shopfront opened an escalation. After yesterday's model patch their rerank results for the same queries have large score deltas (some flipped ordering). They also saw occasional 422 when sending big bundles.

Maya (Support): Here's their minimal repro payload they sent (sensitive fields redacted):
```json
{
  "query": "how to reset checkout filter",
  "items": [
    { "id": "p1", "text": "reset filter in checkout flow" },
    { "id": "p2", "text": "remove filters at checkout" }
  ],
  "model": "reranker-2026-v2.1.3",
  "top_k": 5
}
```

Maya (Support): Their example before patch (v2.1.2) returned scores: p1=0.82, p2=0.56. After v2.1.3 they get p1=0.38, p2=0.72 (so ranks swapped). Customer is very sensitive to ordering.

Maya (Support): Also attached error snippet when they hit a bigger batch (we throttle to 128 docs):
```json
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{ "error": "input exceeds item limit (max 128)" }
```

Diego (ML Eng): Thanks Maya. Can you paste the raw request headers + full body if available? Was the customer hitting dedicated or hosted?

Maya (Support): They're on Dedicated (reserved). I have a redacted request header: `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED-cust-token]`, `X-Model-Version: reranker-2026-v2.1.3`, `Content-Length: 1543`.

Maya (Support): They also provided a local diff they ran:
```text
v2.1.2 scores: [0.82, 0.56]
v2.1.3 scores: [0.38, 0.72]
```

Diego (ML Eng): @Riley @ops-bot any deploys for reranker in the 03:00-04:00 window yesterday? Could be a runtime change (tokenizer/build flags) coupled with model changes.

ops-bot: Deploy event: `rerank-service` rolled out `reranker-2026-v2.1.3` to ded-cluster-3 at 2026-03-02T03:12:07Z by @deploy-bot. Canary passed.

Riley (SRE): I see the deploy. Checking infra logs — there was also a config change to `batching_mask` in the runtime at 03:10 for performance (PR #842). I'll paste the commit hash: `commit: a1b2c3d4` and the change was toggling `normalize_scores=false` in the scorer config to avoid extra L2 ops.

Diego (ML Eng): That normalization toggle rings alarm bells. The ranking model expects L2-normalized embeddings before dot product; turning normalization off will change absolute score magnitudes and can invert ordering in edge cases.

Diego (ML Eng): Repro steps for engineers:
```bash
# fetch model container (internal)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFR_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal-api.redup/rerank/compare?model=v2.1.2" -o before.json
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFR_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal-api.redup/rerank/compare?model=v2.1.3" -o after.json
# run local scorer diff (internal script)
python tools/rerank_diff.py --before before.json --after after.json --query 'how to reset checkout filter'
```

Diego (ML Eng): Quick patch we can try: re-enable `normalize_scores=true` in the runtime config and restart the scorer pods for dedicated clusters. That should restore previous magnitudes.

Riley (SRE): I can roll that change. Rollback plan: either revert the runtime config or rollback the model to v2.1.2 on that customer's route. Rolling runtime config is faster (no model IO).

Riley (SRE): Commands I'll run (internal ops):
```bash
kubectl -n rerank apply -f rerank-config-normalize-true.yaml # toggles normalize_scores=true
k rollout restart deployment/rerank-scorer -n rerank
# smoke test after ~30s: curl local health endpoint
curl -sS http://rerank-scorer.redup.local/health || true
```

Riley (SRE): I'll do a canary to ded-cluster-3 first then propagate. ETA ~30-45m for canary + validation.

Ava (CS): Customer wants an ETA and a temporary mitigation. If we need to rollback model instead I need a short script or docs to give them so they can retry with `model=v2.1.2` as a stopgap.

Diego (ML Eng): Short mitigation for customer (send to them): add `model_version: reranker-2026-v2.1.2` to the request or pin in their Dedicated model routing. That will get old scoring behavior immediately.

Maya (Support): I already suggested the workaround and they prefer us to fix infra since pinning might be tricky for them. They're asking for a clear RCA and timeline.

Diego (ML Eng): Preliminary RCA (short): `normalize_scores` was disabled in runtime to speed up throughput. Combined with subtle tokenizer/embedding changes in v2.1.3 (tokenization edge-case fixed), the change in embed magnitudes led to ordering differences for near-tie items.

Diego (ML Eng): Longer-term fix: 1) re-enable normalization by default for all dedicated clusters; 2) add a unit test in the reranker CI that compares rank-order on a fixed set of queries across model bumps; 3) include score-distribution checks in canary.

Riley (SRE): Patch deployed to canary ded-cluster-3 at 03:47Z. Canary logs show scores align with v2.1.2 for the customer's sample. Smoke output snippet:
```text
Before (v2.1.2) -> [0.82, 0.56]
After (v2.1.3 + normalize=true) -> [0.81, 0.58]
```

Maya (Support): Customer responded: "Thanks — see improvement. Please confirm fully fixed before we close." They asked also about the 422s for big batches.

Diego (ML Eng): 422s are working-as-designed: we enforce max items=128 at API layer. For larger bundles we should return 200 with partial results in future, but for now we must keep limit to protect memory. I'll add a note to docs and product backlog.

Ava (CS): I'll draft a customer-facing note: short summary, mitigation (pin to v2.1.2 or wait for infra fix), ETA ~45m, and offer a postmortem.

Riley (SRE): I'll promote the normalize change to the rest of ded clusters in 2 hours assuming no regressions. Will attach deploy tags and timestamps.

Diego (ML Eng): Followups: add a CI test to fail canary if mean rank-swap rate > 1% for our seeded queries. I'll open PR after lunch.

Maya (Support): I'll keep Shopfront updated. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

Riley (SRE): Monitoring note: set an alert for rerank-order-drift (>0.5% reorder rate) and for sudden change in mean score magnitude. Adding alert to SRE runbook. :rotating_light:

Ava (CS): Please drop the customer-facing summary in #customer-comm once ready so I can review before sending.

Maya (Support): Will do. Closing loop when promoted to all clusters.

(End of thread)
